body: Pershing Square (2004). Structural edge: activist stakes large enough to change boards/management; permanent capital via Pershing Square Holdings (listed 2014) so LPs cannot run. Process: 8-12 simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative businesses with pricing power and low leverage, bought when temporarily mispriced, plus cheap asymmetric macro hedges. Signature wins: General Growth Properties after its 2009 bankruptcy (~$60m into ~$1.6bn+, unverified); Canadian Pacific turnaround 2011-16 (~$2.6bn profit, unverified); Chipotle and Hilton; Feb-Mar 2020 credit default swap hedge that made ~$2.6bn (premium cost ~$27m widely reported but not confirmed here). Biggest mistakes: Valeant 2015-17 - concentrated bet on a roll-up whose growth came from price gouging and acquisitions; ~$4bn loss (CNBC). Herbalife $1bn short (2012-18, loss), JC Penney (2010-13, loss). PSH had four straight losing years 2015-18 before +58% (2019) and +70% (2020) (unverified exact figures). Copyable: own a small number of high-quality compounders bought on temporary bad news; use cheap options/hedges where payoff is many times premium; never let a roll-up's adjusted earnings substitute for organic growth (Valeant lesson maps to Indian acquisition-led stories). Not copyable: activism.

data.copyable: quality concentration on bad news; asymmetric hedges; roll-up skepticism

title: Bill Ackman - concentrated quality activism plus asymmetric hedges
